findings.title: quantize leaks decimal.InvalidOperation instead of a domain error for unrepresentable input
findings.evidence: parse_money accepts any non-float value via 'Decimal(str(value))', so strings such as 'NaN', 'Infinity', or a value larger than the 28-digit context precision reach 'return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)'; quantize raises decimal.InvalidOperation (an ArithmeticError, not TypeError/ValueError) for NaN/Inf and whenever the quantized result exceeds context digits.
findings.recommendation: Validate with amount.is_finite() and catch decimal.InvalidOperation around quantize, re-raising ValueError with a clear message (e.g. unsupported/out-of-range money value) so callers get a documented exception type.

findings.title: Quantity is never type-validated; the guard only does a comparison
findings.evidence: 'if quantity < 0:' assumes a number: a str quantity raises TypeError from the comparison, a bool quantity (True) silently passes as 1, and a float quantity passes the check and only fails later at 'parse_money(unit_price) * quantity' with a TypeError. Three different failure modes for one invalid-argument case.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly reject float/bool/str quantity (e.g. require isinstance(quantity, (int, Decimal)) and not isinstance(quantity, bool)) and raise TypeError with the same strictness parse_money applies to money.

findings.title: Float tax_rate is accepted while float money is rejected, letting binary noise in
findings.evidence: parse_money deliberately refuses floats, but 'Decimal(str(tax_rate))' silently round-trips a float rate, so a computed rate such as 0.1 + 0.05 becomes 0.15000000000000002 and feeds the rounded tax; the module's stated float policy is therefore inconsistent between money and rates.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same float rejection to tax_rate (reuse parse_money-style validation or a shared validator) and document that rates must be str/int/Decimal.

findings.title: No tests shipped for the rounding boundaries this module exists to guarantee
findings.evidence: The change adds only the module; nothing exercises 'return (parse_money(unit_price) * quantity).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)' at the 0.005 boundary, on negative amounts (ROUND_HALF_UP rounds away from zero, so -0.005 becomes -0.01), or with multi-cent unit prices times fractional quantities.
findings.recommendation: Add tests covering half-cent boundaries for positive and negative values, float rejection in parse_money, and line_total/total_with_tax composition (including a float tax_rate case).
